public_rationale: The latest named deadline is December 31, 2029. No reviewed evidence meets the early-resolution rule. ARC Prize's December 2025 assessment is consistent with the earliest checkpoint but does not cover the entire year. Its September 2026 results show substantial progress, while the organizer explicitly declines to call the system AGI. The AGI Society likewise finds the published evidence insufficient. These records neither settle the later timing forecasts nor establish whether scaling alone suffices. Marcus expressed strong skepticism, not certainty, so a binary outcome would also simplify his wording.
limitations: This assessment preserves the separate timing and scaling propositions within one supplied claim.
No single benchmark or organization's assessment establishes universal agreement about AGI.
The undated scaling proposition remains open independently of the 2029 timing deadline.
An observed outcome cannot by itself determine whether an unquantified probability judgment was well calibrated.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: To Marcus, as a cognitive scientist, neither the "scale is all you need" notion nor AGI arriving in 2025 (or 2027 or 2029) seems remotely plausible.
conditions: seems to me as a cognitive scientist

statement.excerpt: Not because I inherently dislike AI, but because I feel like so many folks have been brainwashed by the “scale is all you need” notion and “AGI in 2025” (or 2027 or 2029) nonsense, none of which seems remotely plausible to me as a cognitive scientist.
statement.document_title: Marcus goes gaga over Gates clip

from_speaker: none of which seems remotely plausible to me as a cognitive scientist
our_interpretation: Read as a qualitative forecast expressing strong skepticism about AGI arriving by the named years, alongside skepticism that scaling alone suffices. This is not a categorical claim of impossibility.
Use broadly general human-level cognitive competence as the ordinary meaning of AGI. Marcus supplies no operational definition or benchmark threshold.
Treat the named years as separate year-end checkpoints. The combined claim's latest deadline is December 31, 2029; this does not erase the earlier 2025 and 2027 checkpoints.

Read scaling alone as increasing model size, training data and computation without essential new methods. Whether reinforcement learning, inference-time reasoning or external scaffolding counts as scaling is unspecified.
The timing and scaling propositions are distinct. AGI produced through new methods could count against the timing forecast without contradicting the scaling skepticism.
The phrase about his perspective as a cognitive scientist is a qualification, not a conditional antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: For each timing checkpoint, credible evidence covering the field through that year-end establishes that no qualifying AGI system had appeared. Supporting the separate scaling proposition requires evidence that scaling the existing approach is insufficient; missing a deadline alone does not establish that.
criteria.contradiction_condition: An independently corroborated system with broadly general human-level cognitive competence appears by a named checkpoint. Contradicting the scaling proposition additionally requires technical evidence that scaling alone produced the capability. Such an event would count against the forecast, without logically disproving a subjective low-probability judgment.

evidence.excerpt: So, do we have AGI? Not yet.
evidence.locator: Section The New Meta, concluding paragraph
evidence.explanation: The organizer judged AGI unachieved in early December 2025. This is consistent with Marcus's earliest checkpoint, but cannot establish absence through December 31 or settle the later deadlines.

evidence.excerpt: GPT-6 Astra surpasses the human baseline in action efficiency on ARC-AGI-3.
evidence.explanation: This is material evidence of progress against an overly broad reading of Marcus's skepticism. The same report records 62.7% with the standard harness and 99.9% with a provider adapter, while explicitly declining to identify the system as AGI.

evidence.excerpt: There is no generally accepted empirical test for AGI.
evidence.locator: Section Proposed tests of general intelligence, opening sentence
evidence.explanation: The society reviews September AGI declarations and concludes that published evidence does not yet establish GPT-6 Astra as AGI. This is its assessment of other evaluations, not a new comprehensive test or proof that AGI is absent.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Independent, broad evaluations establishing a qualifying AGI system by a named checkpoint could settle that timing component early. Otherwise, reassess evidence covering each completed year-end, including 2027 and 2029. Resolving the scaling component additionally requires technical evidence separating increased scale from essential new methods.
